findings: BLOCKING EVIDENCE: no downloaded evidence is present, only data modules and generic source URLs. A plan-of-management landing URL, a DOI string and Humboldt/CARDER homepages do not prove any species record or behavior. Actually read each used record/document, preserve source text and identify park-specific occurrence evidence, or remove the unsupported entry.

Sample mountain_river_crabs asserts Pseudothelphusidae in park, behaviors, predators and excellent water quality without cited record-level support. Need actual in-park occurrence evidence, no inference from generic Colombian highland range or water clarity.

Sample little_red_brocket gives exact 2500–3800 m and behavior with only generic pages. Every number requires an official dated supporting passage, and presence must be in park. No nearby-region inference.

Sample black_chested_buzzard_eagle and mountain_tanagers promise what visitor will see and give anatomical/ecological claims without precise support. Retain only supported traits and conditional chances, never guarantees.

Sample spectacled-bear encounter is a safety protocol attributed to general park/Humboldt pages. Use an actual official species-encounter guide, avoid absolute temperament prediction, shorten to clear safe actions; scope remains fauna for encountering wildlife.

Verify DOI 10.15472/r0e1u9 and eBird hotspot L1142279 actually resolve to the intended park data. Record real title, provider, geography, taxon evidence and access date; never fabricate a dataset identity.
Threat categories must distinguish global/national status and assessment year, not conflate CR/VU or sources. Park versus buffer-zone counts must not be presented as one park inventory.

Review ALL 90 entries, including taxonomy names, endemic claims, amphibians/reptiles/insects/crustaceans, numerical counts and derived behavior. Reduce entry count rather than use unsourced species to meet 90; no encyclopedia padding.
